Eilidh —

You asked for proof a stripped‑back product page beats “on brand” and a plan to test it fast. Here’s the beauty before/after, then the exact changes for Sea Buckthorn.

Glow Theory (skincare, DTC) — before/after:
- Before: ads leaned on the homepage and the same few creatives.
- After: 27 new creative variants; two focused product pages, each making a single promise; budget moved to the concepts that kept winning.
- Result: ROAS 1.6 → 3.1 over two 90‑day blocks.
- Note: the winning hero image was a phone shot (serum in a cold sink) that beat a £12k studio shoot.

Sea Buckthorn Glow Serum — fast, stripped‑back v1 (above the fold):
- Title, one‑line promise; bottle shot.
- Price “£24”; primary CTA “Buy 30ml — £24”.
- Express wallets stacked under the main CTA.
- Micro‑proof by the CTA: “As seen by 2M+ on TikTok”, “Fragrance‑free, sensitive‑skin friendly”, “Free UK delivery over £40”.

Variants/OOS (your current blocker):
- Preselect 30ml (in stock).
- Move 15ml “Back in 2 weeks” below the fold with a “Email me when it’s back” link. Don’t lead with it.

Below the fold (tight):
- Order: How to use → Ingredients (collapsed) → Shipping & returns → FAQs.
- Keep “Hand‑poured in Glasgow” as a trust line under the CTA, not between price and button.

How to test quickly:
- Duplicate the page as a “fast” variant with the changes above.
- Route paid/social traffic to the fast variant; leave organic on the current page.
- Measure first orders (and cost per first order) from those sources; shift spend when the fast page wins.

Immediate wins today:
- Default 30ml; relabel the primary button “Buy 30ml — £24”.
- Pull delivery threshold and TikTok proof up under the CTA.
